plain: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, tells of a 1968 paper by Northrop, a big American aircraft maker, about using electric charge to help move or lift aircraft, an idea tied to the inventor Townsend Brown, and links it to talk of electric charging on the wings of the B-2, a stealth bomber. He says that when a researcher named Dan Marcas went looking for the paper in an aerospace journal, it had completely vanished. The writer Nick Cook also recalls such Northrop papers but places them, unsure, in the early 1960s, and the vanishing matters to the tellers because it would suggest the work was pulled into secrecy.
